principles.statement: Things which are equal to the same thing are also equal to one another.

principles.statement: When a straight line set up on a straight line makes the adjacent angles equal to one another, each of the equal angles is right, and the straight line standing on the other is called a perpendicular to that on which it stands.

principles.statement: An obtuse angle is an angle greater than a right angle.
principles.title: Euclid I.def.11

principles.statement: An acute angle is an angle less than a right angle.
principles.title: Euclid I.def.12

principles.statement: A boundary is that which is an extremity of anything.

principles.statement: A figure is that which is contained by any boundary or boundaries.
principles.title: Euclid I.def.14

principles.statement: A circle is a plane figure contained by one line such that all the straight lines falling upon it from one point among those lying within the figure are equal to one another.
principles.title: Euclid I.def.15

principles.statement: And the point is called the centre of the circle.
principles.title: Euclid I.def.16

principles.statement: A diameter of the circle is any straight line drawn through the centre and terminated in both directions by the circumference of the circle, and such a straight line also bisects the circle.

principles.statement: A semicircle is the figure contained by the diameter and the circumference cut off by it. And the centre of the semicircle is the same as that of the circle.
principles.title: Euclid I.def.18

principles.statement: Rectilineal figures are those which are contained by straight lines, trilateral figures being those contained by three, quadrilateral those contained by four, and multilateral those contained by more than four straight lines.
principles.title: Euclid I.def.19

principles.statement: A line is breadthless length.
principles.title: Euclid I.def.2

principles.statement: Of trilateral figures, an equilateral triangle is that which has its three sides equal, an isosceles triangle that which has two of its sides alone equal, and a scalene triangle that which has its three sides unequal.
principles.title: Euclid I.def.20

principles.statement: Further, of trilateral figures, a right-angled triangle is that which has a right angle, an obtuse-angled triangle that which has an obtuse angle, and an acute-angled triangle that which has its three angles acute.
principles.title: Euclid I.def.21

principles.statement: Of quadrilateral figures, a square is that which is both equilateral and right-angled ; an oblong that which is right-angled but not equilateral ; a rhombus that which is equilateral but not right-angled ; and a rhomboid that which has its opposite sides and angles equal to one another but is neither equilateral nor right-angled. And let quadrilaterals other than these be called trapezia.
principles.title: Euclid I.def.22

principles.statement: Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet one another in either direction.
principles.title: Euclid I.def.23

principles.statement: The extremities of a line are points.
principles.title: Euclid I.def.3

principles.statement: A straight line is a line which lies evenly with the points on itself.
principles.title: Euclid I.def.4

principles.statement: A surface is that which has length and breadth only.
principles.title: Euclid I.def.5

principles.statement: The extremities of a surface are lines.
principles.title: Euclid I.def.6

principles.statement: A plane surface is a surface which lies evenly with the straight lines on itself.
principles.title: Euclid I.def.7

principles.statement: A plane angle is the inclination to one another of two lines in a plane which meet one another and do not lie in a straight line.
principles.title: Euclid I.def.8

principles.statement: And when the lines containing the angle are straight, the angle is called rectilineal.
principles.title: Euclid I.def.9

principles.statement: Given two straight lines constructed on a straight line (from its extremities) and meeting in a point, there cannot be constructed on the same straight line (from its extremities), and on the same side of it, two other straight lines meeting in another point and equal to the former two respectively, namely each to that which has the same extremity with it.
principles.title: Euclid I.7

principles.statement: Any rectangular parallelogram is said to be contained by the two straight lines containing the right angle.
principles.title: Euclid II.def.1

principles.statement: And in any parallelogrammic area let any one whatever of the parallelograms about its diameter with the two complements be called a gnomon.
principles.title: Euclid II.def.2

principles.statement: If there be two straight lines, and one of them be cut into any number of segments whatever, the rectangle contained by the two straight lines is equal to the rectangles contained by the uncut straight line and each of the segments.
principles.title: Euclid II.1

principles.statement: If a straight line be bisected, and a straight line be added to it in a straight line, the square on the whole with the added straight line and the square on the added straight line both together are double of the square on the half and of the square described on the straight line made up of the half and the added straight line as on one straight line.
principles.title: Euclid II.10

principles.statement: To cut a given straight line so that the rectangle contained by the whole and one of the segments is equal to the square on the remaining segment.
principles.title: Euclid II.11

principles.statement: In obtuse-angled triangles the square on the side subtending the obtuse angle is greater than the squares on the sides con- taining the obtuse angle by twice the rectangle contained by one of the sides about the obtuse angle, namely that on which the
principles.title: Euclid II.12

principles.statement: In acute-angled triangles the square on the side subtending the acute angle is less than the squares on the sides containing the acute angle by twice the rectangle contained by one of the sides about the acute angle, namely that on which the per- pendicular falls, and the straight line cut off within by the perpendicular towards the acute angle.
principles.title: Euclid II.13

principles.statement: To construct a square equal to a given rectilineal figure.
principles.title: Euclid II.14

principles.statement: If a straight line be cut at random, the rectangle contained by the whole and both of the segments is equal to the square on the whole.
principles.title: Euclid II.2

principles.statement: If a straight line be cut at random, the rectangle contained by the whole and one of the segments is equal to the rectangle contained by the segments and the square on the aforesaid segment.
principles.title: Euclid II.3

principles.statement: If a straight line be cut at random, the square on the whole is equal to the squares on the segments and twice the rectangle contained by the segments.
principles.title: Euclid II.4

principles.statement: If a straight line be cut into equal and unequal segments, the rectangle contained by the unequal segments of the whole together with the square on the straight line between the points of section is equal to the square on the half.
principles.title: Euclid II.5

principles.statement: If a straight line be bisected and a straight line be added to it in a straight line, the rectangle contained by the whole with the added straight line and the added straight line together with the square on the half is equal to the square on the straight line made up of the half and the added straight line.
principles.title: Euclid II.6

principles.statement: If a straight line be cut at random, the square on the whole and that on one of the segments both together are equal to twice the rectangle contained by the whole and the said segment and the square on the remaining segment.
principles.title: Euclid II.7

principles.statement: If a straight line be cut at random, four times the rectangle contained by the whole and one of the segments together with the square on the remaining segment is equal to the square described on the whole and the aforesaid segment as on one straight line.
principles.title: Euclid II.8

principles.statement: If a straight line be cut into equal and unequal segments, the squares on the unequal segments of the whole are double of the square on the half and of the square on the straight line between the points of section.
principles.title: Euclid II.9

principles.statement: Equal circles are those the diameters of which are equal, or the radii of which are equal.
principles.title: Euclid III.def.1

principles.statement: A sector of a circle is the figure which, when an angle is constructed at the centre of the circle, is contained by the straight lines containing the angle and the circumference cut off by them.
principles.title: Euclid III.def.10

principles.statement: Similar segments of circles are those which admit equal angles, or in which the angles are equal to one another.
principles.title: Euclid III.def.11

principles.statement: A straight line is said to touch a circle which, meeting the circle and being produced, does not cut the circle.
principles.title: Euclid III.def.2

principles.statement: Circles are said to touch one another which, meeting one another, do not cut one another.
principles.title: Euclid III.def.3

principles.statement: In a circle straight lines are said to be equally distant from the centre when the perpendiculars drawn to them from the centre are equal.
principles.title: Euclid III.def.4

principles.statement: And that straight line is said to be at a greater distance on which the greater perpendicular falls.
principles.title: Euclid III.def.5

principles.statement: A segment of a circle is the figure contained by a straight line and a circumference of a circle.
principles.title: Euclid III.def.6

principles.statement: An angle of a segment is that contained by a straight line and a circumference of a circle.
principles.title: Euclid III.def.7

principles.statement: An angle in a segment is the angle which, when a point is taken on the circumference of the segment and straight lines are joined from it to the extremities of the straight line which is the base of the segment, is contained by the straight lines so joined.
principles.title: Euclid III.def.8

principles.statement: And, when the straight lines containing the angle cut off a circumference, the angle is said to stand upon that circumference.
principles.title: Euclid III.def.9

principles.statement: A circle does not cut a circle at more points than two.
principles.title: Euclid III.10

principles.statement: If two circles touch one another internally, and their centres be taken, the straight line joining their centres, if it be also produced, will fall on the point of contact of the circles.
principles.title: Euclid III.11

principles.statement: If two circles touch one another externally, the straight line joining their centres will pass through the point of contact.
principles.title: Euclid III.12

principles.statement: A circle does not touch a circle at more points than one, whether it touch it internally or externally.
principles.title: Euclid III.13

principles.statement: In a circle equal straight lines are equally distant from the centre, and those which are equally distant from the centre are equal to one another.
principles.title: Euclid III.14

principles.statement: Of straight lines in a circle the diameter is greatest, and of the rest the nearer to the centre is always greater than the more remote.
principles.title: Euclid III.15

principles.statement: The straight line drawn at right angles to the diameter of a circle from its extremity will fall outside the circle, and into the space between the straight line and the circumference another straight line cannot be interposed; further the angle of the semicircle is greater, and the remaining angle less, than any acute rectilineal angle.
principles.title: Euclid III.16

principles.statement: If a straight line touch a circle, and a straight line be joined from the centre to the point of contact, the straight line so joined will be perpendicular to the tangent.
principles.title: Euclid III.18

principles.statement: If a straight line touch a circle, and from the point of contact a straight line be drawn at right angles to the tangent, the centre of the circle will be on the straight line so drawn.
principles.title: Euclid III.19

principles.statement: If on the circumference of a circle two points be taken at random, the straight line joining the points will fall within the circle.
principles.title: Euclid III.2

principles.statement: On the same straight line there cannot be constructed two similar and unequal segments of circles on the same side.
principles.title: Euclid III.23

principles.statement: Similar segments of circles on equal straight lines are equal to one another.
principles.title: Euclid III.24

principles.statement: Given a segment of a circle, to describe the complete circle of which it is a segment.
principles.title: Euclid III.25

principles.statement: In equal circles equal angles stand on equal circumferences, whether they stand at the centres or at the circumferences.
principles.title: Euclid III.26

principles.statement: In equal circles angles standing on equal circumferences are equal to one another, whether they stand at the centres or at the circumferences.
principles.title: Euclid III.27

principles.statement: In equal circles equal straight lines cut off equal circumferences, the greater equal to the greater and the less to the less.
principles.title: Euclid III.28

principles.statement: In equal circles equal circumferences are subtended by equal straight lines.
principles.title: Euclid III.29

principles.statement: If in a circle a straight line through the centre bisect a straight line not through the centre, it also cuts it at right angles; and if it cut it at right angles, it also bisects it.
principles.title: Euclid III.3

principles.statement: To bisect a given circumference.
principles.title: Euclid III.30

principles.statement: On a given straight line to describe a segment of a circle admitting an angle equal to a given rectilineal angle.
principles.title: Euclid III.33

principles.statement: From a given circle to cut off a segment admitting an angle equal to a given rectilineal angle.
principles.title: Euclid III.34

principles.statement: If a point be taken outside a circle and from the point there fall on the circle two straight lines, if one of them cut the circle, and the other fall on it, and if further the rectangle contained by the whole of the straight line which cuts
principles.title: Euclid III.37

principles.statement: If in a circle two straight lines cut one another which are not through the centre, they do not bisect one another.
principles.title: Euclid III.4

principles.statement: If two circles cut one another, they will not have the same centre.
principles.title: Euclid III.5

principles.statement: If two circles touch one another, they will not have the same centre.
principles.title: Euclid III.6

principles.statement: If on the diameter of a circle a point be taken which is not the centre of the circle, and from the point straight lines fall upon the circle, that will be greatest on which the centre is, the remainder of the same diameter will be least, and of the rest the nearer to the straight line through the centre is always greater than the more remote, and only two equal straight lines will fall from the point on the circle, one on each side of the least straight line.
principles.title: Euclid III.7

principles.statement: If a point be taken outside a circle and from the point straight lines be drawn through to the circle, one of which is through the centre and the others are drawn at random, then, of the straight lines which fall on the concave circumference, that through the centre is greatest, while of the rest
principles.title: Euclid III.8

principles.statement: If a point be taken within a circle, and more than two equal straight lines fall from the point on the circle, the point taken is the centre of the circle.
principles.title: Euclid III.9

principles.statement: A rectilineal figure is said to be inscribed in a rectilineal figure when the respective angles of the inscribed figure lie on the respective sides of that in which it is inscribed.
principles.title: Euclid IV.def.1

principles.statement: Similarly a figure is said to be circumscribed about a figure when the respective sides of the circumscribed figure pass through the respective angles of that about which it is circumscribed.
principles.title: Euclid IV.def.2

principles.statement: A rectilineal figure is said to be inscribed in a circle when each angle of the inscribed figure lies on the circumference of the circle.
principles.title: Euclid IV.def.3

principles.statement: A rectilineal figure is said to be circumscribed about a circle, when each side of the circumscribed figure touches the circumference of the circle.
principles.title: Euclid IV.def.4

principles.statement: Similarly a circle is said to be inscribed in a figure when the circumference of the circle touches each side of the figure in which it is inscribed.
principles.title: Euclid IV.def.5

principles.statement: A circle is said to be circumscribed about a figure when the circumference of the circle passes through each angle of the figure about which it is circumscribed.
principles.title: Euclid IV.def.6

principles.statement: A straight line is said to be fitted into a circle when its extremities are on the circumference of the circle.
principles.title: Euclid IV.def.7

principles.statement: Into a given circle to fit a straight line equal to a given straight line which is not greater than the diameter of the circle.
principles.title: Euclid IV.1

principles.statement: To construct an isosceles triangle having each of the angles at the base double of the remaining one.
principles.title: Euclid IV.10

principles.statement: In a given circle to inscribe an equilateral and equiangular pentagon.
principles.title: Euclid IV.11

principles.statement: About a given circle to circumscribe an equilateral and equiangular pentagon.
principles.title: Euclid IV.12

principles.statement: In a given pentagon, which is equilateral and equiangular, to inscribe a circle.
principles.title: Euclid IV.13

principles.statement: About a given pentagon, which is equilateral and equiangular, to circumscribe a circle.
principles.title: Euclid IV.14

principles.statement: In a given circle to inscribe an equilateral and equiangular hexagon.
principles.title: Euclid IV.15

principles.statement: In a given circle to inscribe a fifteen-angled figure which shall be both equilateral and equiangular.
principles.title: Euclid IV.16

principles.statement: In a given circle to inscribe a triangle equiangular with a given triangle.
principles.title: Euclid IV.2

principles.statement: About a given circle to circumscribe a triangle equiangular with a given triangle.
principles.title: Euclid IV.3

principles.statement: In a given triangle to inscribe a circle.
principles.title: Euclid IV.4

principles.statement: About a given triangle to circumscribe a circle.
principles.title: Euclid IV.5

principles.statement: In a given circle to inscribe a square.
principles.title: Euclid IV.6

principles.statement: About a given circle to circumscribe a square.
principles.title: Euclid IV.7

principles.statement: In a given square to inscribe a circle.
principles.title: Euclid IV.8

principles.statement: About a given square to circumscribe a circle.
principles.title: Euclid IV.9

principles.statement: Similar rectilineal figures are such as have their angles severally equal and the sides about the equal angles proportional.
principles.title: Euclid VI.def.1

principles.statement: [2. Reciprocally related figures. See note.]
principles.title: Euclid VI.def.2

principles.statement: A straight line is said to have been cut in extreme and mean ratio when, as the whole line is to the greater segment, so is the greater to the less.
principles.title: Euclid VI.def.3

principles.statement: The height of any figure is the perpendicular drawn from the vertex to the base.
principles.title: Euclid VI.def.4

principles.statement: Triangles and parallelograms which are under the same height are to one another as their bases.
principles.title: Euclid VI.1

principles.statement: To cut a given uncut straight line similarly to a given cut straight line.
principles.title: Euclid VI.10

principles.statement: To three given straight lines to find a fourth proportional.
principles.title: Euclid VI.12

principles.statement: In equal and equiangular parallelograms the sides about the equal angles are reciprocally proportional; and equiangular parallelograms in which the sides about the equal angles are reciprocally proportional are equal.
principles.title: Euclid VI.14

principles.statement: In equal triangles which have one angle equal to one angle the sides about the equal angles are reciprocally proportional; and those triangles which have one angle equal to one angle, and in which the sides about the equal angles are reciprocally proportional, are equal.
principles.title: Euclid VI.15

principles.statement: If four straight lines be proportional, the rectangle contained by the extremes is equal to the rectangle contained by the means; and, if the rectangle contained by the extremes be equal to the rectangle contained by the means, the four straight lines will be proportional.
principles.title: Euclid VI.16

principles.statement: If three straight lines be proportional, the rectangle contained by the extremes is equal to the square on the mean; and, if the rectangle contained by the extremes be equal to the square on the mean, the three straight lines will be proportional.

¬(b.sameSide d M)  -- ******** -- 2 -- If L, M, and N are lines meeting at a point a, and b, c, and d are points -- on L, M, and N respectively, and if c and d are on the same side of L, -- and b and d are not on the same side of M, and d is not on M and b != a, -- then b and c are on the same side of N -- ******** axiom triple_incidence_2 : ∀ (L M N : Line) (a b c d : Point), (a.onLine L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (a.onLine N) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine M) ∧ (d.onLine N) ∧ (c.sameSide d L) ∧ ¬(b.sameSide d M) ∧ ¬(d.onLine M) ∧ (b ≠ a) → b.sameSide c N  -- ******** -- 3 -- If L, M, and N are lines meeting at a point a, and b, c, and d are points -- on L, M, and N respectively, and if c and d are on the same side of L, -- and b and c are on the same side of N, and d and e are on the same side -- of M, and c and e are on the same side of N, then c and e are on the same -- side of L -- ******** axiom triple_incidence_3 : ∀ (L M N : Line) (a b c d e : Point), (a.onLine L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (a.onLine N) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine M) ∧ (d.onLine N) ∧ (c.sameSide d L) ∧ (b.sameSide c N) ∧ (d.sameSide e M) ∧ (c.sameSide e N) → c.sameSide e L  -- ******** circle axioms ********  -- ******** -- 1 -- If a, b, and c are on L, a is inside α, b and c are on α, and b != c, then a -- -- is a. between bnd c -- -- ******** axiom circle_line_intersections : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line) (α : Circle), (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine L) ∧ (a.insideCircle α) ∧ (b.onCircle α) ∧ (c.onCircle α) ∧ (b ≠ c) → between b a c  -- ******** -- 2 -- If a and b are each inside α or on α, and c is  between a and b, then c is -- inside α -- ********  axiom circle_points_between : ∀ (a b c : Point) (α : Circle), ¬(a.outsideCircle α) ∧ ¬(b.outsideCircle α) ∧ (between a c b) → c.insideCircle α  -- ******** -- 3 -- If a is inside α or on α, c is not inside α, and c is  between a and b, then b -- is neither inside α nor on α -- ******** axiom circle_points_extend : ∀ (a b c : Point) (α : Circle), ¬(a.outsideCircle α) ∧ ¬(c.insideCircle α) ∧ (between a c b) → (b.outsideCircle α)  -- ******** -- 4  Let α and β be distinct circles that intersect in distinct points c and d -- Let a be a the centre of α, let b be the centre of β, and let L be the line -- through a and b  Then c and d are not on the same side of L -- ********  axiom circles_intersections_diff_side : ∀ (a b c d : Point) (α β : Circle) (L : Line), (α ≠ β) ∧ (c.onCircle α) ∧ (c.onCircle β) ∧ (d.onCircle α) ∧ (d.onCircle β) ∧ (c ≠ d) ∧ (a.isCentre α) ∧ (b.isCentre β) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) → ¬(c.sameSide d L)  -- ******** intersection rules ********  -- ******** -- 1 -- If a and b are on different sides of L, and M is the line through a and b, -- then L and M intersect -- ******** axiom intersection_lines_opposing: ∀ (a b : Point) (L M : Line), (a.opposingSides b L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (b.onLine M) → L.intersectsLine M  -- /-- -- Not in [Avigad et al., 2009] -- -/ axiom intersection_lines_common_point : ∀ (a : Point) (L M : Line), a.onLine L ∧ a.onLine M ∧ L ≠ M → L.intersectsLine M  -- /-- -- Not in [Avigad et al., 2009] -- -/ axiom parallel_line_unique : ∀ (a : Point) (L M N : Line), ¬(a.onLine L) ∧ a.onLine M ∧ a.onLine N ∧ ¬(L.intersectsLine M) ∧ ¬(L.intersectsLine N) → M = N  -- /-- -- Not in [Avigad et al., 2009] -- -/  axiom intersection_symm : ∀ (L M : Line), L.intersectsLine M → M.intersectsLine L  -- ******** -- 2 -- If a is on or inside α, b is on or inside α, and a and b are on different sides -- of L, then L and α intersect -- ******** axiom intersection_circle_line_1: ∀ (a b : Point) (α : Circle) (L: Line), ¬(a.outsideCircle α) ∧ ¬(b.outsideCircle α) ∧ (a.opposingSides b L) → L.intersectsCircle α  -- ******** -- 3  If a is inside α and on L, then L and α intersect -- ******** axiom intersection_circle_line_2: ∀ (a : Point) (α : Circle) (L: Line), (a.insideCircle α) ∧ (a.onLine L) → L.intersectsCircle α  -- ******** -- 4  If a is on or inside α, b is on or inside α, a is inside β, and b is outside β, -- then α and β intersect -- ********  axiom intersection_circle_circle_1: ∀ (a b : Point) (α β : Circle), (a.onCircle α) ∧ ¬(b.outsideCircle α) ∧ (a.insideCircle β) ∧ (b.outsideCircle β) → α.intersectsCircle β  -- ******** -- 5  If a is on α, b is in α, a is in β, and b is on β, then α and β intersect -- ******** axiom intersection_circle_circle_2: ∀ (a b : Point) (α β : Circle), (a.onCircle α) → (b.insideCircle α) → (a.insideCircle β) → (b.onCircle β) → α.intersectsCircle β  -- ******** parallelogram rules ******** -- /-- -- Not in [Avigad et al., 2009] --

-- If a is the centre of α then a is inside α -- ********  axiom center_inside_circle : ∀ (a : Point) (α : Circle), a.isCentre α → a.insideCircle α  -- ******** -- 4 -- If (a : Point) is inside (α : Circle), then a is not on α -- -- ******** axiom inside_not_on_circle : ∀ (a : Point) (α : Circle), a.insideCircle α → ¬(a.onCircle α)  -- ********  between axioms ********  -- ******** -- 1 -- If b is  between a and c then b is  between c and a, a != b, a != c, and a is -- not a. between bnd c -- ******** axiom between_symm : ∀ (a b c : Point), between a b c → (between c b a) ∧ (a ≠ b) ∧ (a ≠ c) ∧ ¬(between b a c)  -- ******** -- 2 -- If b is  between a and c, a is on L, and b is on L, then c is on L -- ********  axiom between_same_line_out : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (between a b c) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) → c.onLine L  -- ******** -- 3  If b is  between a and c, a is on L, and c is on L, then b is on L -- ********  axiom between_same_line_in : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (between a b c) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine L) → b.onLine L  -- -- ******** -- 4 -- If b is  between a and c and d is  between a and b then d is  between a and c -- -- ******** axiom between_trans_in : ∀ (a b c d : Point), (between a b c) ∧ (between a d b) → between a d c  -- ******** -- 5 -- If b is  between a and c and c is a. between bnd d then b is  between a and d -- ********  -- -- ******** axiom between_trans_out : ∀ (a b c d : Point), (between a b c) ∧ (between b c d) → (between a b d)  -- ******** -- 6 -- If a, b, and c are distinct points on a line L, then then either b is  between -- a and c, or a is a. between bnd c, or c is  between a and b -- ********  axiom between_points : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (a ≠ b) ∧ (b ≠ c) ∧ (c ≠ a) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine L) → (between a b c) ∨ (between b a c) ∨ (between a c b)  -- ******** -- 7 -- If b is  between a and c and b is  between a and d then b is not  between c -- and d -- ******** axiom between_not_trans : ∀ (a b c d : Point), (between a b c) ∧ (between a b d) → ¬(between c b d)  -- ******** same side axioms ********  -- ******** -- 1 -- If a is not on L, then a and a are on the same side of L -- ******** axiom same_side_rfl : ∀ (a : Point) (L : Line), ¬(a.onLine L) → a.sameSide a L  -- ******** -- 2 -- If a and b are on the same side of L, then b and a are on the same side of L -- ******** axiom same_side_symm : ∀ (a b : Point) (L : Line), a.sameSide b L → b.sameSide a L  -- ******** -- 3 -- If a and b are on the same side of L, then a is not on L -- ******** axiom same_side_not_on_line : ∀ (a b : Point) (L : Line), a.sameSide b L → ¬(a.onLine L)  -- ******** -- 4 -- If a and b are on the same side of L, and a and c are on the same side of -- L, then b and c are on the same side of L -- -- ******** axiom same_side_trans : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (a.sameSide b L) ∧ (a.sameSide c L) → b.sameSide c L  -- ******** -- 5 -- If a, b, and c are not on L, and a and b are not on the same side of L, -- then either a and c are on the same side of L, or b and c are on the same -- side of L -- ******** axiom same_side_pigeon_hole : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), ¬(a.onLine L) ∧ ¬(b.onLine L) ∧ ¬(c.onLine L) → (a.sameSide b L) ∨ (a.sameSide c L) ∨ (b.sameSide c L)  -- ******** -- 1 -- If b is  between a and c and a and c are on the same side of L, then a and -- b are on the same side of L -- ******** axiom pasch_1: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (between a b c) ∧ (a.sameSide c L) → a.sameSide b L  -- ******** -- 2 -- If b is  between a and c and a is on L and b is not on L, then b and c are -- on the same side of L -- -- ******** axiom pasch_2: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (between a b c) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ ¬(b.onLine L) → b.sameSide c L  -- ******** -- 3 -- If b is  between a and c and b is on L then a and c are not on the same -- side of L -- ******** -- -- See also Avigad's notes on this rule (https://www.andrew.cmu.edu/user/avigad/Papers/euclid_notes.htm) axiom pasch_3: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (between a b c) ∧ (b.onLine L) → ¬(a.sameSide c L)  -- ******** -- 4 -- If b is the intersection of distinct lines L and M, a and c are distinct points -- on M, a != b, c != b, and a and c are not on the same side of L, then b is --  between a and c -- ********  axiom pasch_4: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L M : Line), (L ≠ M) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine M) ∧ distinctPointsOnLine a c M ∧ (a ≠ b) ∧ (c ≠ b) ∧ ¬(a.sameSide c L) → between a b c  -- ******** triple incidence axioms ********  -- ******** -- 1 -- If L, M, and N are lines meeting at a point a, and axiom triple_incidence_1 : ∀ (L M N : Line) (a b c d : Point), (a.onLine L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (a.onLine N) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine M) ∧ (d.onLine N) ∧ (c.sameSide d L) ∧ (b.sameSide c N) → d are not on the same side of M, and d is not on M and b != a, -- then b and c are on the same side of N -- ******** axiom triple_incidence_2 : ∀ (L M N : Line) (a b c d : Point), (a.onLine L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (a.onLine N) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine M) ∧ (d.onLine N) ∧ (c.sameSide d L) ∧ ¬(b.sameSide d M) ∧ ¬(d.onLine M) ∧ (b ≠ a) → b.sameSide c N  -- ******** -- 3 -- If L, M, and N are lines meeting at a point a, and b, c, and d are points -- on L, M, and N respectively, and if c and d are on the same side of L, -- and b and c are on the same side of N, and d and e are on the same side -- of M, and c and e are on the same side of N, then c and e are on the same -- side of L -- ******** axiom triple_incidence_3 : ∀ (L M N : Line) (a b c d e : Point), (a.onLine L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (a.onLine N) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine M) ∧ (d.onLine N) ∧ (c.sameSide d L) ∧ (b.sameSide c N) ∧ (d.sameSide e M) ∧ (c.sameSide e N) → c.sameSide e L  -- ******** circle axioms ********  -- ******** -- 1 -- If a, b, and c are on L, a is inside α, b and c are on α, and b != c, then a -- -- is a. between bnd c -- -- ******** axiom circle_line_intersections : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line) (α : Circle), (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine L) ∧ (a.insideCircle α) ∧ (b.onCircle α) ∧ (c.onCircle α) ∧ (b ≠ c) → between b a c  -- ******** -- 2 -- If a and b are each inside α or on α, and c is  between a and b, then c is -- inside α -- ********  axiom circle_points_between : ∀ (a b c : Point) (α : Circle), ¬(a.outsideCircle α) ∧ ¬(b.outsideCircle α) ∧ (between a c b) → c.insideCircle α  -- ******** -- 3 -- If a is inside α or on α, c is not inside α, and c is  between a and b, then b -- is neither inside α nor on α -- ******** axiom circle_points_extend : ∀ (a b c : Point) (α : Circle), ¬(a.outsideCircle α) ∧ ¬(c.insideCircle α) ∧ (between a c b) → (b.outsideCircle α)  -- ******** -- 4  Let α and β be distinct circles that intersect in distinct points c and d -- Let a be a the centre of α, let b be the centre of β, and let L be the line -- through a and b  Then c and d are not on the same side of L -- ********  axiom circles_intersections_diff_side : ∀ (a b c d : Point) (α β : Circle) (L : Line), (α ≠ β) ∧ (c.onCircle α) ∧ (c.onCircle β) ∧ (d.onCircle α) ∧ (d.onCircle β) ∧ (c ≠ d) ∧ (a.isCentre α) ∧ (b.isCentre β) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) → ¬(c.sameSide d L)  -- ******** intersection rules ********  -- ******** -- 1 -- If a and b are on different sides of L, and M is the line through a and b, -- then L and M intersect -- ******** axiom intersection_lines_opposing: ∀ (a b : Point) (L M : Line), (a.opposingSides b L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (b.onLine M) → L.intersectsLine M  -- /-- -- Not in [Avigad et al., 2009] -- -/ axiom intersection_lines_common_point : ∀ (a : Point) (L M : Line), a.onLine L ∧ a.onLine M ∧ L ≠ M → L.intersectsLine M  -- /-- -- Not in [Avigad et al., 2009] -- -/ axiom parallel_line_unique : ∀ (a : Point) (L M N : Line), ¬(a.onLine L) ∧ a.onLine M ∧ a.onLine N ∧ ¬(L.intersectsLine M) ∧ ¬(L.intersectsLine N) → M = N  -- /-- -- Not in [Avigad et al., 2009] -- -/  axiom intersection_symm : ∀ (L M : Line), L.intersectsLine M → M.intersectsLine L  -- ******** -- 2 -- If a is on or inside α, b is on or inside α, and a and b are on different sides -- of L, then L and α intersect -- ******** axiom principles.statement: If points `a` and `b` are both centers of `(α : Circle)` then `a = b` -/ axiom centre_unique : ∀ (a b : Point) (α : Circle), (a.isCentre α) ∧ (b.isCentre α) → a = b  -- ******** -- 3 -- If a is the centre of α then a is inside α -- ********  axiom center_inside_circle : ∀ (a : Point) (α : Circle), a.isCentre α → a.insideCircle α  -- ******** -- 4 -- If (a : Point) is inside (α : Circle), then a is not on α -- -- ******** axiom inside_not_on_circle : ∀ (a : Point) (α : Circle), a.insideCircle α → ¬(a.onCircle α)  -- ********  between axioms ********  -- ******** -- 1 -- If b is  between a and c then b is  between c and a, a != b, a != c, and a is -- not a. between bnd c -- ******** axiom between_symm : ∀ (a b c : Point), between a b c → (between c b a) ∧ (a ≠ b) ∧ (a ≠ c) ∧ ¬(between b a c)  -- ******** -- 2 -- If b is  between a and c, a is on L, and b is on L, then c is on L -- ********  axiom between_same_line_out : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (between a b c) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) → c.onLine L  -- ******** -- 3  If b is  between a and c, a is on L, and c is on L, then b is on L -- ********  axiom between_same_line_in : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (between a b c) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine L) → b.onLine L  -- -- ******** -- 4 -- If b is  between a and c and d is  between a and b then d is  between a and c -- -- ******** axiom between_trans_in : ∀ (a b c d : Point), (between a b c) ∧ (between a d b) → between a d c  -- ******** -- 5 -- If b is  between a and c and c is a. between bnd d then b is  between a and d -- ********  -- -- ******** axiom between_trans_out : ∀ (a b c d : Point), (between a b c) ∧ (between b c d) → (between a b d)  -- ******** -- 6 -- If a, b, and c are distinct points on a line L, then then either b is  between -- a and c, or a is a. between bnd c, or c is  between a and b -- ********  axiom between_points : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (a ≠ b) ∧ (b ≠ c) ∧ (c ≠ a) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine L) → (between a b c) ∨ (between b a c) ∨ (between a c b)  -- ******** -- 7 -- If b is  between a and c and b is  between a and d then b is not  between c -- and d -- ******** axiom between_not_trans : ∀ (a b c d : Point), (between a b c) ∧ (between a b d) → ¬(between c b d)  -- ******** same side axioms ********  -- ******** -- 1 -- If a is not on L, then a and a are on the same side of L -- ******** axiom same_side_rfl : ∀ (a : Point) (L : Line), ¬(a.onLine L) → a.sameSide a L  -- ******** -- 2 -- If a and b are on the same side of L, then b and a are on the same side of L -- ******** axiom same_side_symm : ∀ (a b : Point) (L : Line), a.sameSide b L → b.sameSide a L  -- ******** -- 3 -- If a and b are on the same side of L, then a is not on L -- ******** axiom same_side_not_on_line : ∀ (a b : Point) (L : Line), a.sameSide b L → ¬(a.onLine L)  -- ******** -- 4 -- If a and b are on the same side of L, and a and c are on the same side of -- L, then b and c are on the same side of L -- -- ******** axiom same_side_trans : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (a.sameSide b L) ∧ (a.sameSide c L) → b.sameSide c L  -- ******** -- 5 -- If a, b, and c are not on L, and a and b are not on the same side of L, -- then either a and c are on the same side of L, or b and c are on the same -- side of L -- ******** axiom same_side_pigeon_hole : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), ¬(a.onLine L) ∧ ¬(b.onLine L) ∧ ¬(c.onLine L) → (a.sameSide b L) ∨ (a.sameSide c L) ∨ (b.sameSide c L)  -- ******** -- 1 -- If b is  between a and c and a and c are on the same side of L, then a and -- b are on the same side of L -- ******** axiom pasch_1: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (between a b c) ∧ (a.sameSide c L) → a.sameSide b L  -- ******** -- 2 -- If b is  between a and c and a is on L and b is not on L, then b and c are -- on the same side of L -- -- ******** axiom pasch_2: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (between a b c) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ ¬(b.onLine L) → b.sameSide c L  -- ******** -- 3 -- If b is  between a and c and b is on L then a and c are not on the same -- side of L -- ******** -- -- See also Avigad's notes on this rule (https://www.andrew.cmu.edu/user/avigad/Papers/euclid_notes.htm) axiom pasch_3: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (between a b c) ∧ (b.onLine L) → ¬(a.sameSide c L)  -- ******** -- 4 -- If b is the intersection of distinct lines L and M, a and c are distinct points -- on M, a != b, c != b, and a and c are not on the same side of L, then b is --  between a and c -- ********  axiom pasch_4: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L M : Line), (L ≠ M) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine M) ∧ distinctPointsOnLine a c M ∧ (a ≠ b) ∧ (c ≠ b) ∧ ¬(a.sameSide c L) → between a b c  -- ******** triple incidence axioms ********  -- ******** -- 1 -- If L, M, and N are lines meeting at a point a, and b, c, and d are points -- on L, M, and N respectively, and if c and d are on the same side of L, -- and b and c are on the same side of N, then b and d are not on the same -- side of M -- ******** axiom triple_incidence_1 : ∀ (L M N : Line) (a b c d : Point), (a.onLine L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (a.onLine N) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine M) ∧ (d.onLine N) ∧ (c.sameSide d L) ∧ (b.sameSide c N) → ¬(b.sameSide d M)  -- ******** -- 2 -- If L, M, and N are lines meeting at a point a, and b, c, and d are points -- on L, M, and N respectively, and if c and d are on the same side of L, -- and b and d are not on the same side of M, and d is not on M and b != a, -- then b and c are on the same side of N -- ******** axiom triple_incidence_2 : ∀ (L M N : Line) (a b c d : Point), (a.onLine L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (a.onLine N) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine M) ∧ (d.onLine N) ∧ (c.sameSide d L) ∧ ¬(b.sameSide d M) ∧ ¬(d.onLine M) ∧ (b ≠ a) → b.sameSide c N  -- ******** -- 3 -- If L, M, and N are lines meeting at a point a, and b, c, and d are points -- on L, M, and N respectively, and if c and d are on the same side of L, -- and b and c are on the same side of N, and d and e are on the same side -- of M, and c and e are on the same side of N, then c and e are on the same -- side of L -- ******** axiom triple_incidence_3 : ∀ (L M N : Line) (a b c d e : Point), (a.onLine L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (a.onLine N) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine M) ∧ (d.onLine N) ∧ (c.sameSide d L) ∧ (b.sameSide c N) ∧ (d.sameSide e M) ∧ (c.sameSide e N) → c.sameSide e L  -- ******** circle axioms ********  -- ******** -- 1 -- If a, b, and c are on L, a is inside α, b and c are on α, and b != c, then a -- -- is a. between bnd c -- -- ******** axiom circle_line_intersections : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line) (α : Circle), (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine L) ∧ (a.insideCircle α) ∧ (b.onCircle α) ∧ (c.onCircle α) ∧ (b ≠ c) → between b a c  -- ******** -- 2 -- If a and b are each inside α or on α, and c is  between a and b, then c is -- inside α -- ********  axiom circle_points_between : ∀ (a b c : Point) (α : Circle), ¬(a.outsideCircle α) ∧ ¬(b.outsideCircle α) ∧ (between a c b) → c.insideCircle α  -- ******** -- 3 -- If a is inside α or on α, c is not inside α, and c is  between a and b, then b -- is neither inside α nor on α -- ******** axiom circle_points_extend : ∀ (a b c : Point) (α : Circle), ¬(a.outsideCircle α) ∧ ¬(c.insideCircle α) ∧ (between a c b) → (b.outsideCircle α)  -- ******** -- 4  Let α and β be distinct circles that intersect in distinct points c and d -- Let a be a the centre of α, let b be the centre of β, and let L be the line -- through a and b  Then c and d are not on the same side of L -- ********  axiom circles_intersections_diff_side : ∀ (a b c d : Point) (α β : Circle) (L : Line), (α ≠ β) ∧ (c.onCircle α) ∧ (c.onCircle β) ∧ (d.onCircle α) ∧ (d.onCircle β) ∧ (c ≠ d) ∧ (a.isCentre α) ∧ (b.isCentre β) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) → ¬(c.sameSide d L)  -- ******** intersection rules ********  -- ******** -- 1 -- If a and b are on different sides of L, and M is the line through a and b, -- then L and M intersect -- ******** axiom intersection_lines_opposing: ∀ (a b : Point) (L M : Line), (a.opposingSides b L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (b.onLine M) → L.intersectsLine M  -- /-- -- Not in [Avigad et al., 2009] --

L) → (between a b c) ∨ (between b a c) ∨ (between a c b)  -- ******** -- 7 -- If b is  between a and c and b is  between a and d then b is not  between c -- and d -- ******** axiom between_not_trans : : ∀ (a b : Point) (L : Line), a.sameSide b L → ¬(a.onLine L)  -- ******** -- 4 -- If a and b are on the same side of L, and a and c are on the same side of -- L, then b and c are on the same side of L -- -- ******** axiom same_side_trans : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (a.sameSide b L) ∧ (a.sameSide c L) → b.sameSide c L  -- ******** -- 5 -- If a, b, and c are not on L, and a and b are not on the same side of L, -- then either a and c are on the same side of L, or b and c are on the same -- side of L -- ******** axiom same_side_pigeon_hole : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), ¬(a.onLine L) ∧ L, then b and c are -- on the same side of L -- -- ******** axiom pasch_2: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (between a b c) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ ¬(b.onLine L) → b.sameSide c L  -- ******** -- 3 -- If b is  between a and c and b is on L then a and c are not on the same -- side of L -- ******** -- -- See also Avigad's notes on this rule (https://www.andrew.cmu.edu/user/avigad/Papers/euclid_notes.htm) on M, a != b, c != b, and a and c are not on the same side of L, then b is --  between a and c -- ********  axiom pasch_4: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L M : Line), (L ≠ M) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine M) ∧ distinctPointsOnLine a c M ∧ (a ≠ b) ∧ (c ≠ b) ∧ ¬(a.sameSide c L) → between a b c  -- ******** triple incidence axioms ********  -- ******** -- 1 -- If L, M, and N are lines meeting at a point a, and b, c, and d are points -- on L, M, and N respectively, and if c and d are on the same side of L, -- and b and c are on the same side of N, then b and d are not on the same -- side of M -- ******** axiom triple_incidence_1 : ∀ (L M N : Line) (a b c d : Point), (a.onLine L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (a.onLine N) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine M) ∧ (d.onLine N) ∧ (c.sameSide d L) ∧ (b.sameSide c N) → ¬(b.sameSide d M)  -- ******** -- 2 -- If L, M, and N are lines meeting at a point a, and b, c, and d are points -- on L, M, and N respectively, and if c and d are on the same side of L, -- and b and d are not on the same side of M, and d is not on M and b != a, -- then b and c are on the same side of N -- ******** axiom triple_incidence_2 : ∀ (L M N : Line) (a b c d : Point), (a.onLine L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (a.onLine N) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine M) ∧ (d.onLine N) ∧ (c.sameSide d L) ∧ ¬(b.sameSide d M) ∧ ¬(d.onLine M) ∧ (b ≠ a) → b.sameSide c N  -- ******** -- 3 -- If L, M, and N are lines meeting at a point a, and b, c, and d are points -- on L, M, and N respectively, and if c and d are on the same side of L, -- and b and c are on the same side of N, and d and e are on the same side -- of M, and c and e are on the same side of N, then c and e are on the same -- side of L -- ******** axiom triple_incidence_3 : ∀ (L M N : Line) (a b c d e : Point), (a.onLine L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (a.onLine N) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine M) ∧ (d.onLine N) ∧ (c.sameSide d L) ∧ (b.sameSide c N) ∧ (d.sameSide e M) ∧ (c.sameSide e N) → c.sameSide e L  -- ******** circle axioms ********  -- ******** Circle), (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine L) ∧ (a.insideCircle α) ∧ (b.onCircle α) ∧ (c.onCircle α) ∧ (b ≠ c) → between b a c  -- ******** -- 2 -- If a and b are each inside α or on α, and c is ******** -- 3 -- If a is inside α or on α, c is not inside α, and c is  between a and b, then b -- is neither inside α nor on α -- ******** axiom circle_points_extend : ∀ (a b c : Point) (α : Circle), ¬(a.outsideCircle α) ∧ ¬(c.insideCircle α) ∧ (between a c b) → (b.outsideCircle α)  -- ******** -- 4  Let α and β be distinct circles that intersect in distinct points c and d -- Let a be a the centre of α, let b be the centre of β, and let L be the line -- through a and b  Then c and d are not on the same side of L -- ********  axiom circles_intersections_diff_side : ∀ (a b c d : Point) (α β : Circle) (L : Line), (α ≠ β) ∧ (c.onCircle α) ∧ (c.onCircle β) ∧ (d.onCircle α) ∧ (d.onCircle β) ∧ (c ≠ d) ∧ (a.isCentre α) ∧ (b.isCentre β) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) → ¬(c.sameSide d L)  -- ******** intersection rules ********  -- ******** -- 1 -- If a and b are on different sides of L, and M is the line through a and b, -- then L and M intersect -- ******** axiom intersection_lines_opposing: ∀ (a b : Point) (L M : Line), (a.opposingSides b L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (b.onLine M) → L.intersectsLine M  -- /-- -- Not in [Avigad et al., 2009] --

axiom between_trans_out : ∀ (a b c d : Point), (between a b c) ∧ (between b c d) → (between a b d)  -- ******** -- 6 -- If a, b, and c are distinct points on a line L, then then either b is  between -- a and c, or a is a. between bnd c, or c is  between a and b -- ********  axiom between_points : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (a ≠ b) ∧ (b ≠ c) ∧ (c ≠ a) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine L) → (between a b c) ∨ (between b a c) ∨ (between a c b)  -- ******** -- 7 -- If b is  between a and c and b is  between a and d then b is not  between c -- and d -- ******** axiom between_not_trans : ∀ (a b c d : Point), (between a b c) ∧ (between a b d) → ¬(between c b d)  -- ******** same side axioms ********  -- ******** -- 1 -- If a is not on L, then a and a are on the same side of L -- ******** axiom same_side_rfl : ∀ (a : Point) (L : Line), ¬(a.onLine L) → a.sameSide a L  -- ******** -- 2 -- If a and b are on the same side of L, then b and a are on the same side of L -- ******** axiom same_side_symm : ∀ (a b : Point) (L : Line), a.sameSide b L → b.sameSide a L  -- ******** -- 3 -- If a and b are on the same side of L, then a is not on L -- ******** axiom same_side_not_on_line : ∀ (a b : Point) (L : Line), a.sameSide b L → ¬(a.onLine L)  -- ******** -- 4 -- If a and b are on the same side of L, and a and c are on the same side of -- L, then b and c are on the same side of L -- -- ******** axiom same_side_trans : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (a.sameSide b L) ∧ (a.sameSide c L) → b.sameSide c L  -- ******** -- 5 -- If a, b, and c are not on L, and a and b are not on the same side of L, -- then either a and c are on the same side of L, or b and c are on the same -- side of L -- ******** axiom same_side_pigeon_hole : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), ¬(a.onLine L) ∧ ¬(b.onLine L) ∧ ¬(c.onLine L) → (a.sameSide b L) ∨ (a.sameSide c L) ∨ (b.sameSide c L)  -- ******** -- 1 -- If b is  between a and c and a and c are on the same side of L, then a and -- b are on the same side of L -- ******** axiom pasch_1: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (between a b c) ∧ (a.sameSide c L) → a.sameSide b L  -- ******** -- 2 -- If b is  between a and c and a is on L and b is not on L, then b and c are -- on the same side of L -- -- ******** axiom pasch_2: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (between a b c) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ ¬(b.onLine L) → b.sameSide c L  -- ******** -- 3 -- If b is  between a and c and b is on L then a and c are not on the same -- side of L -- ******** -- -- See also Avigad's notes on this rule (https://www.andrew.cmu.edu/user/avigad/Papers/euclid_notes.htm) axiom pasch_3: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (between a b c) ∧ (b.onLine L) → ¬(a.sameSide c L)  -- ******** -- 4 -- If b is the intersection of distinct lines L and M, a and c are distinct points -- on M, a != b, c != b, and a and c are not on the same side of L, then b is --  between a and c -- ********  axiom pasch_4: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L M : Line), (L ≠ M) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine M) ∧ distinctPointsOnLine a c M ∧ (a ≠ b) ∧ (c ≠ b) ∧ ¬(a.sameSide c L) → between a b c  -- ******** triple incidence axioms ********  -- ******** -- 1 -- If L, M, and N are lines meeting at a point a, and b, c, and d are points -- on L, M, and N respectively, and if c and d are on the same side of L, -- and b and c are on the same side of N, then b and d are not on the same -- side of M -- ******** axiom triple_incidence_1 : ∀ (L M N : Line) (a b c d : Point), (a.onLine L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (a.onLine N) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine M) ∧ (d.onLine N) ∧ (c.sameSide d L) ∧ (b.sameSide c N) → ¬(b.sameSide d M)  -- ******** -- 2 -- If L, M, and N are lines meeting at a point a, and b, c, and d are points -- on L, M, and N respectively, and if c and d are on the same side of L, -- and b and d are not on the same side of M, and d is not on M and b != a, -- then b and c are on the same side of N -- ******** axiom triple_incidence_2 : ∀ (L M N : Line) (a b c d : Point), (a.onLine L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (a.onLine N) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine M) ∧ (d.onLine N) ∧ (c.sameSide d L) ∧ ¬(b.sameSide d M) ∧ ¬(d.onLine M) ∧ (b ≠ a) → b.sameSide c N  -- ******** -- 3 -- If L, M, and N are lines meeting at a point a, and b, c, and d are points -- on L, M, and N respectively, and if c and d are on the same side of L, -- and b and c are on the same side of N, and d and e are on the same side -- of M, and c and e are on the same side of N, then c and e are on the same -- side of L -- ******** axiom triple_incidence_3 : ∀ (L M N : Line) (a b c d e : Point), (a.onLine L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (a.onLine N) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine M) ∧ (d.onLine N) ∧ (c.sameSide d L) ∧ (b.sameSide c N) ∧ (d.sameSide e M) ∧ (c.sameSide e N) → c.sameSide e L  -- ******** circle axioms ********  -- ******** -- 1 -- If a, b, and c are on L, a is inside α, b and c are on α, and b != c, then a -- -- is a. between bnd c -- -- ******** axiom circle_line_intersections : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line) (α : Circle), (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine L) ∧ (a.insideCircle α) ∧ (b.onCircle α) ∧ (c.onCircle α) ∧ (b ≠ c) → between b a c  -- ******** -- 2 -- If a and b are each inside α or on α, and c is  between a and b, then c is -- inside α -- ********  axiom circle_points_between : ∀ (a b c : Point) (α : Circle), ¬(a.outsideCircle α) ∧ ¬(b.outsideCircle α) ∧ (between a c b) → c.insideCircle α  -- ******** -- 3 -- If a is inside α or on α, c is not inside α, and c is  between a and b, then b -- is neither inside α nor on α -- ******** axiom circle_points_extend : ∀ (a b c : Point) (α : Circle), ¬(a.outsideCircle α) ∧ ¬(c.insideCircle α) ∧ (between a c b) → (b.outsideCircle α)  -- ******** -- 4  Let α and β be distinct circles that intersect in distinct points c and d -- Let a be a the centre of α, let b be the centre of β, and let L be the line -- through a and b  Then c and d are not on the same side of L -- ********  axiom circles_intersections_diff_side : ∀ (a b c d : Point) (α β : Circle) (L : Line), (α ≠ β) ∧ (c.onCircle α) ∧ (c.onCircle β) ∧ (d.onCircle α) ∧ (d.onCircle β) ∧ (c ≠ d) ∧ (a.isCentre α) ∧ (b.isCentre β) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) → ¬(c.sameSide d L)  -- ******** intersection rules ********  -- ******** -- 1 -- If a and b are on different sides of L, and M is the line through a and b, -- then L and M intersect -- ******** axiom intersection_lines_opposing: ∀ (a b : Point) (L M : Line), (a.opposingSides b L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (b.onLine M) → L.intersectsLine M  -- /-- -- Not in [Avigad et al., 2009] -- -/ axiom intersection_lines_common_point : ∀ (a : Point) (L M : Line), a.onLine L ∧ a.onLine M ∧ L ≠ M → L.intersectsLine M  -- /-- -- Not in [Avigad et al., 2009] -- -/ axiom parallel_line_unique : ∀ (a : Point) (L M N : Line), ¬(a.onLine L) ∧ a.onLine M ∧ a.onLine N ∧ ¬(L.intersectsLine M) ∧ ¬(L.intersectsLine N) → M = N  -- /-- -- Not in [Avigad et al., 2009] --

principles.statement: If points `a` and `b` are both centers of `(α : Circle)` then `a = b` -/ axiom centre_unique : ∀ (a b : Point) (α : Circle), (a.isCentre α) ∧ (b.isCentre α) → a = b  -- ******** -- 3 -- If a is the centre of α then a is inside α -- ********  axiom center_inside_circle : ∀ (a : Point) (α : Circle), a.isCentre α → a.insideCircle α  -- ******** -- 4 -- If (a : Point) is inside (α : Circle), then a is not on α -- -- ******** axiom inside_not_on_circle : ∀ (a : Point) (α : Circle), a.insideCircle α → ¬(a.onCircle α)  -- ********  between axioms ********  -- ******** -- 1 -- If b is  between a and c then b is  between c and a, a != b, a != c, and a is -- not a. between bnd c -- ******** axiom between_symm : ∀ (a b c : Point), between a b c → (between c b a) ∧ (a ≠ b) ∧ (a ≠ c) ∧ ¬(between b a c)  -- ******** -- 2 -- If b is  between a and c, a is on L, and b is on L, then c is on L -- ********  axiom between_same_line_out : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (between a b c) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) → c.onLine L  -- ******** -- 3  If b is  between a and c, a is on L, and c is on L, then b is on L -- ********  axiom between_same_line_in : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (between a b c) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine L) → b.onLine L  -- -- ******** -- 4 -- If b is  between a and c and d is  between a and b then d is  between a and c -- -- ******** axiom between_trans_in : ∀ (a b c d : Point), (between a b c) ∧ (between a d b) → between a d c  -- ******** -- 5 -- If b is  between a and c and c is a. between bnd d then b is  between a and d -- ********  -- -- ******** axiom between_trans_out : ∀ (a b c d : Point), (between a b c) ∧ (between b c d) → (between a b d)  -- ******** -- 6 -- If a, b, and c are distinct points on a line L, then then either b is  between -- a and c, or a is a. between bnd c, or c is  between a and b -- ********  axiom between_points : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (a ≠ b) ∧ (b ≠ c) ∧ (c ≠ a) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine L) → (between a b c) ∨ (between b a c) ∨ (between a c b)  -- ******** -- 7 -- If b is  between a and c and b is  between a and d then b is not  between c -- and d -- ******** axiom between_not_trans : ∀ (a b c d : Point), (between a b c) ∧ (between a b d) → ¬(between c b d)  -- ******** same side axioms ********  -- ******** -- 1 -- If a is not on L, then a and a are on the same side of L -- ******** axiom same_side_rfl : ∀ (a : Point) (L : Line), ¬(a.onLine L) → a.sameSide a L  -- ******** -- 2 -- If a and b are on the same side of L, then b and a are on the same side of L -- ******** axiom same_side_symm : ∀ (a b : Point) (L : Line), a.sameSide b L → b.sameSide a L  -- ******** -- 3 -- If a and b are on the same side of L, then a is not on L -- ******** axiom same_side_not_on_line : ∀ (a b : Point) (L : Line), a.sameSide b L → ¬(a.onLine L)  -- ******** -- 4 -- If a and b are on the same side of L, and a and c are on the same side of -- L, then b and c are on the same side of L -- -- ******** axiom same_side_trans : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (a.sameSide b L) ∧ (a.sameSide c L) → b.sameSide c L  -- ******** -- 5 -- If a, b, and c are not on L, and a and b are not on the same side of L, -- then either a and c are on the same side of L, or b and c are on the same -- side of L -- ******** axiom same_side_pigeon_hole : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), ¬(a.onLine L) ∧ ¬(b.onLine L) ∧ ¬(c.onLine L) → (a.sameSide b L) ∨ (a.sameSide c L) ∨ (b.sameSide c L)  -- ******** -- 1 -- If b is  between a and c and a and c are on the same side of L, then a and -- b are on the same side of L -- ******** axiom pasch_1: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (between a b c) ∧ (a.sameSide c L) → a.sameSide b L  -- ******** -- 2 -- If b is  between a and c and a is on L and b is not on L, then b and c are -- on the same side of L -- -- ******** axiom pasch_2: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (between a b c) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ ¬(b.onLine L) → b.sameSide c L  -- ******** -- 3 -- If b is  between a and c and b is on L then a and c are not on the same -- side of L -- ******** -- -- See also Avigad's notes on this rule (https://www.andrew.cmu.edu/user/avigad/Papers/euclid_notes.htm) axiom pasch_3: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (between a b c) ∧ (b.onLine L) → ¬(a.sameSide c L)  -- ******** -- 4 -- If b is the intersection of distinct lines L and M, a and c are distinct points -- on M, a != b, c != b, and a and c are not on the same side of L, then b is --  between a and c -- ********  axiom pasch_4: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L M : Line), (L ≠ M) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine M) ∧ distinctPointsOnLine a c M ∧ (a ≠ b) ∧ (c ≠ b) ∧ ¬(a.sameSide c L) → between a b c  -- ******** triple incidence axioms ********  -- ******** -- 1 -- If L, M, and N are lines meeting at a point a, and b, c, and d are points -- on L, M, and N respectively, and if c and d are on the same side of L, -- and b and c are on the same side of N, then b and d are not on the same -- side of M -- ******** axiom triple_incidence_1 : ∀ (L M N : Line) (a b c d : Point), (a.onLine L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (a.onLine N) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine M) ∧ (d.onLine N) ∧ (c.sameSide d L) ∧ (b.sameSide c N) → ¬(b.sameSide d M)  -- ******** -- 2 -- If L, M, and N are lines meeting at a point a, and b, c, and d are points -- on L, M, and N respectively, and if c and d are on the same side of L, -- and b and d are not on the same side of M, and d is not on M and b != a, -- then b and c are on the same side of N -- ******** axiom triple_incidence_2 : ∀ (L M N : Line) (a b c d : Point), (a.onLine L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (a.onLine N) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine M) ∧ (d.onLine N) ∧ (c.sameSide d L) ∧ ¬(b.sameSide d M) ∧ ¬(d.onLine M) ∧ (b ≠ a) → b.sameSide c N  -- ******** -- 3 -- If L, M, and N are lines meeting at a point a, and b, c, and d are points -- on L, M, and N respectively, and if c and d are on the same side of L, -- and b and c are on the same side of N, and d and e are on the same side -- of M, and c and e are on the same side of N, then c and e are on the same -- side of L -- ******** axiom triple_incidence_3 : ∀ (L M N : Line) (a b c d e : Point), (a.onLine L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (a.onLine N) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine M) ∧ (d.onLine N) ∧ (c.sameSide d L) ∧ (b.sameSide c N) ∧ (d.sameSide e M) ∧ (c.sameSide e N) → c.sameSide e L  -- ******** circle axioms ********  -- ******** -- 1 -- If a, b, and c are on L, a is inside α, b and c are on α, and b != c, then a -- -- is a. between bnd c -- -- ******** axiom circle_line_intersections : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line) (α : Circle), (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine L) ∧ (a.insideCircle α) ∧ (b.onCircle α) ∧ (c.onCircle α) ∧ (b ≠ c) → between b a c  -- ******** -- 2 -- If a and b are each inside α or on α, and c is  between a and b, then c is -- inside α -- ********  axiom circle_points_between : ∀ (a b c : Point) (α : Circle), ¬(a.outsideCircle α) ∧ ¬(b.outsideCircle α) ∧ (between a c b) → c.insideCircle α  -- ******** -- 3 -- If a is inside α or on α, c is not inside α, and c is  between a and b, then b -- is neither inside α nor on α -- ******** axiom circle_points_extend : ∀ (a b c : Point) (α : Circle), ¬(a.outsideCircle α) ∧ ¬(c.insideCircle α) ∧ (between a c b) → (b.outsideCircle α)  -- ******** -- 4  Let α and β be distinct circles that intersect in distinct points c and d -- Let a be a the centre of α, let b be the centre of β, and let L be the line -- through a and b  Then c and d are not on the same side of L -- ********  axiom circles_intersections_diff_side : ∀ (a b c d : Point) (α β : Circle) (L : Line), (α ≠ β) ∧ (c.onCircle α) ∧ (c.onCircle β) ∧ (d.onCircle α) ∧ (d.onCircle β) ∧ (c ≠ d) ∧ (a.isCentre α) ∧ (b.isCentre β) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) → ¬(c.sameSide d L)  -- ******** intersection rules ********  -- ******** -- 1 -- If a and b are on different sides of L, and M is the line through a and b, -- then L and M intersect -- ******** axiom intersection_lines_opposing: ∀ (a b : Point) (L M : Line), (a.opposingSides b L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (b.onLine M) → L.intersectsLine M  -- /-- -- Not in [Avigad et al., 2009] -- -/ axiom intersection_lines_common_point : ∀ (a : Point) (L M : Line), a.onLine L ∧ a.onLine M ∧ L ≠ M → L.intersectsLine M  -- /-- -- Not in [Avigad et al., 2009] --
